summary: A specialist in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, Masaharu Imai studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1961–1970). He held posts at Ibaraki University (~1977–1991) and the University of Tsukuba (~1991–2005).

Working in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Masahide Mori studied at Nagoya University, University of London, and SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski. He held posts at Nagoya University, Koyasan University (1994), and Kanazawa University (~1996–2007).
Masahiro Asada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1964–1974) and served as an assistant professor (助教授) there (~1984–1993).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Masahiro Inami completed doctoral coursework at Hiroshima University. He held positions at Tokyo Gakugei University (attested ~1991 and ~2004) and taught Hisataka Ishida.

Specializing in religious and Buddhist studies, Masahiro Kusunoki studied at Tohoku University (-1953) and served as a professor there (~1974–1985). He also held posts with the Japanese Association for Religious Studies and Tohoku Association of Indian and Religious Studies.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Masahiro Shimoda completed his degrees at the University of Tokyo, where he was later professor (attested 1991–2015). He also held visiting appointments at Josai, SOAS, Stanford, and the University of Virginia.
Masahiro Takano is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he worked as a librarian (attested 1995).

An Indology and religious studies scholar, Masakazu Tanaka studied at Tohoku University (~1974–1979) and earned his Ph.D. from the London School of Economics (~1981–1986). He held a post at Kyoto University from 1988 to 2019.

Masako Keta, a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, studied at Kyoto University (~1972–1980). She held posts at Aichi University of Technology Automotive Junior College, Kanazawa University, and as Professor für Religionsphilosophie at Kyoto University (~2000–2019).

A Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, Masamichi Ichigo studied at Otani University, Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, Susumu Yamaguchi, and Yuichi Kajiyama, and Michigan. He held posts at Kyoto Sangyo, Otani, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.
Working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Masamichi Sakai studied at the University of Vienna, receiving a doctorate (attested 2010) under the supervision of Helmut Krasser.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Masanori Nakagawa held positions at Chikushi Jogakuen University as a lecturer (attested 1991) and as an assistant professor (助教授) in the Faculty of Literature (attested 2002).

Masanori Shono specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He has held positions as an assistant professor (助教) at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2015).

Masao Abe was a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at Osaka City University and Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe. He held long-term posts at Nara University of Education, as well as Kyoto University and Pacific School of Religion.
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology, Masao Shizutani held assistant professor (助教授) positions at Josai University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).

A scholar of Japanology and religious studies, Masao Yamaguchi studied at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo Metropolitan University. He held positions at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Shizuoka, Sapporo University, and Chuo University.

Masaru Akimoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who held posts at Kyoto Women's University, including as a professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Society (attested 2002, 2015).
Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1965–1974) and later served there as an assistant professor (助教授) from ~1987 to 2017.

A linguist and Indologist, Masato Kobayashi studied at Kyoto University and completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona. He served as a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2003).
A scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, Masatoshi Konishi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1961) and held a post at Rikkyo University from ~1972 to 2004.
